To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the smart home field is in need of a paradigm shift from technology-centered to human-centered design.

the future smart home will be a home that adapts to its occupants and the world around it, that it will be a home with a complex, dynamic and adaptive physical and digital space, and that it will be one where people, technology, and home will collaborate in order to support a wide range of activities.

smart home technology should be: 1) Meaningful: smart homes should be useful and enjoyable to live in; 2) Simple: smart homes should not require extensive training to use and should support the users in their daily activities; 3) Flexible: smart homes should allow for changes in user needs, activities, and technology over time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of homes that are both smart and liveable.
the design of smart home technologies that are more meaningful, that better accommodate the complexity of domestic life, and that support more collaborative relationships between humans and homes.
understanding how to make homes smart in ways that benefit people, and how to do so without compromising the home as a place of comfort, security, and privacy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the future is bright.
the smart home vision is not yet ready.
the smart home vision is still alive and kicking, but that the way to get there has to be different from the one that has been taken so far.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the smart home field has made significant progress in developing technologies for the home, but that we now need to focus more on how to make these technologies meaningful and beneficial to the people living in these homes.
the field of smart homes has come a long way, but there is a lot more work to be done before we will see smart homes that are as useful as we have envisioned.
we envision homes that are not only smart but also meaningful and collaborative.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the smart homes of the future will be augmented homes, and that we need to move beyond smart home visions to augmented home visions to make progress.
the smart homes of tomorrow will be augmented, but not smart, and that the research agenda for home automation should shift accordingly.
we must move from a vision of smart homes that are technologically advanced to one that is technologically unobtrusive.
